messages:
anya: FYI — validator started hard-rejecting structured outputs for /v1/generate on friday night. we got a flood of alerts and the router fell back to the small-model pool which spiked unit cost. attaching a tiny sample from logs.
anya: ```json\n{"request_id":"r-9a3","route":"/v1/generate","error":"schema_mismatch","validator":"output_shape","details":{"missing":"choices[0].metadata.tags"}}\n```
ben: ugh. was the strictness flag flipped in the canary? i thought we decided soft by default.
maria: last deploy notes said canary toggle = enable_strict_validation=true for 10% of traffic. did we accidentally ramp to 100%?
anya: looks like the rollout job retried and applied to entire cluster after a k8s label mismatch. so yes — strict ended up global.
sam: that's rough. two immediate things: (1) revert strictness to soft globally to stop hard rejects and pager churn, (2) add lightweight telemetry counters so we can see soft_reject vs hard_reject and fallback_routed per-route.
ben: agreed. also we should avoid routing every hard_reject to the smallest model variant — that was our safety net but it backfires on volume. maybe route to the same model but with debug flags + sample to disk.
maria: +1. customers got 500-ish errors in logs: "schema_reject" was surfaced. we need graceful degrade that returns model output with a warning field rather than an error for noncritical schema gaps.
anya: proposal for route config in console / yaml (quick):
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
validation_mode: soft   # soft | hard
fallback_policy: preserve_model  # preserve_model | downgraded_pool
reject_response: false # when soft, return output + warnings
telemetry_sample_rate: 0.01
```
sam: nice. adding telemetry we should expose two new metrics: "validator.validation_mode" (enum), "validator.reject_count" (counter, tags: route, mode, reject_type), and "router.fallback_count" (counter, tags: route, target_pool). plus a sampled log event with request_id and failing_path.
ben: also include a small histogram of token_length_at_failure. recent failures look correlated with long prefix lengths.
infra-bot: deploy-bot queued job r-deploy-1123 to rollback canary flag -> soft_validation for cluster:gpu-prod.
maria: long-term UX: make it trivial in Console to flip validation_mode per-route with a canary slider (0-100%). currently the rollback requires stack edits and a deploy.
anya: agree. for now, can we patch the router to not treat hard_reject as immediate route-to-cheapest? add a policy: if reject_rate > X% in 1m, throttle fallback and instead respond with warning to caller to avoid cost shock.
sam: i can PR a conservative change: if fallback_count_in_1m > 1000 then cap fallback_rate to 10% and push others to warning path. will instrument counters and a kill-switch.
ben: timeline? this is affecting billing tonight.
sam: I'll open PR in 20m and request urgent review. plan: hotfix -> patch -> canary 5% -> global in 2h if no regression.
maria: can someone add a dashboard tile: validator rejects over time (split mode: soft/hard), fallback_count, and a per-route error surface. put in the SRE runbook for paging thresholds.
anya: adding noise-control: sample 1% of reject payloads to low-priority storage bucket for debugging. don't dump everything.
ben: note: we must also audit the rollout job that retried. probably a retry-on-failure loop with wrong label selector. I'll take that postmortem.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: r-deploy-1123 rollback applied to 7/9 nodes, remaining nodes draining.
maria: after rollback, exception rate dropped ~85% for the route. cost spike still around for next billing window but trending down.
anya: thanks team. action items: sam -> PR (hotfix for fallback cap + metrics), ben -> audit rollout job, maria -> dashboard + runbook, anya -> sample logs and confirm revert fully rolled. check back in 1h. :thumbsup:
ben: on it.
sam: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/p/infra/+/3456 — marking as urgent. will ping when CI green.
infra-bot: deployment r-deploy-1123 completed, health checks OK.
maria: saw one lingering customer error; support is on it. overall looks stable.
anya: we'll keep this thread for follow-ups; moving UX enhancements (console canary slider) to a separate ticket. thanks everyone.
